title: Alien bodies and egg-shaped UFOs detailed as Pentagon releases new files
excerpt: The Pentagon put out a new batch of previously classified documents detailing encounters with mystical creatures, UFO sightings and more.
content:
The Pentagon put out a new batch of previously classified documents detailing encounters with mystical creatures, UFO sightings and more.

13:00 ET, Fri, Oct 23, 2026

Black triangles illustration

The US government released its seventh batch of documents related to UFO sightings and witness accounts.

This time, the reports — ranging from the 1940s until the present year — include an alleged alien crash.

(Image: US DOW / SWNS)

The White House has released its seventh batch of declassified UFO files this Friday, including a Roswell witness's account of an alleged alien crash and mysterious figures in the sky.

The document is filled with reports of "unidentified anomalous phenomena," collected starting in the 1940s and spanning the decades through 2026.

Despite not containing proof of alien life, the reports include what are described by the FBI and the Pentagon as mysterious black triangular-shaped objects hovering over secret U.S. military sites.

The White House released new documents

Since February 2026, the Trump administration's Department of Defense and other federal agencies have been releasing records tied to UFOs and alien life, in a move a White House spokesperson described as an effort toward government transparency.

This Friday, the Pentagon released the seventh batch of documents on the topic to NewsNation, including sightings of "unidentified anomalous phenomena" ranging from the 1940s to 2026.

The batch reportedly details a Roswell witness's account of an alleged alien crash and mysterious black triangles.

(Image: Getty)

The Roswell incident

The released files shed more light on the Roswell incident from 1947, in which rancher W.W. "Mac" Brazel found strange wreckage, including tinfoil, rubber, tape, and balsa sticks, on a ranch near Corona and Roswell.

The documents contain a sworn statement from an officer present there, who, according to the Daily Mail, could be Walter G. Haut, the base's public information officer, who died in 2005.

The witness, whose name is redacted in the files, claimed to be "convinced" that what he saw was "some type of craft and its crew from outer space."

(Image: Getty)

Roswell witness report

The unidentified witness said they were taken to a guarded hangar, where they saw an egg-shaped craft about 12 to 15 feet long and 6 feet wide, with a metallic surface.

They said the structure had no windows, wings, tail, or landing gear, and was made of a foil he called "paper-thin yet extremely strong."

Nearby, they claimed 4-foot-tall bodies, about the size of a 10-year-old child but with abnormally large heads, lay under a canvas tarpaulin.

(Image: Getty)

They considered deliberately diverting attention

They detailed that there were two sites with debris — one about 75 miles northwest of Roswell and another 40 miles north, of which the latter was considered more important for containing the craft and the bodies.

"No one was able to identify the crash debris," he wrote of the wreckage samples passed around the table, adding that officials had a meeting to decide whether to publicize the ranch debris site to divert attention from the northern one.

Finally, they decided to issue a press release stating that the military had recovered a "flying disk," which they later clarified was a weather balloon.

(Image: Getty)
